extracted.intended_audience: undergraduate or beginning graduate students studying multivariable calculus / real analysis
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, existence theorems, and calculation formulas for arc length, integrals with respect to arc length, and line integrals on parametrically defined curves in R^n, including sufficient conditions (e.g., tamely behaved, bounded derivative) that guarantee rectifiability and Riemann-integral formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple arc (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A simple arc in R^n is a one-one continuous function γ from a closed bounded interval of the line into R^n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to avoid retracing; reparametrizations of simple arcs have the same image. Orientation-preserving vs orientation-reversing reparametrizations are distinguished by where endpoints map (ϕ(a1)=a2 or ϕ(a1)=b2). Examples: different parametrizations of the quarter circle are reparametrizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reparametrization equivalence (Proposition 3.36)
rubrics_metrics.description: If γ1 and γ2 are simple arcs in R^n with the same image, then they are reparametrizations of one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses continuity, compactness, and existence of continuous inverses on the common image. This justifies treating length and many integrals as geometric (image-dependent) rather than parametrization-dependent, provided reparametrization is orientation-preserving where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arc length (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The arc length `(γ)` of a simple arc γ is the supremum over all partitions P of the sum `(γ(P))` of lengths of the line segments joining consecutive image points; γ is rectifiable if `(γ)` is finite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notation: `(γ(P))` = sum_j |γ(t_j) − γ(t_{j−1})| for partition P = {t_j}. Properties: length depends only on the image; adding partition points does not decrease the polygonal sum; additivity over subintervals; reversal of parametrization preserves length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient condition for rectifiability (Proposition 3.37)
rubrics_metrics.description: If γ : [a,b] → R^n has derivative γ'(t) existing for a < t < b and γ'(t) is bounded on (a,b), then γ is rectifiable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses Mean Value Theorem on components to bound polygonal sums by n^{1/2} M (b−a). Caveats: this condition can be too strong (examples show reparametrization can remove unboundedness) and not necessary (some curves with unbounded derivative are rectifiable after reparametrization), and some examples show existence of derivative everywhere but nonrectifiability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polygonal approximation properties (observations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic inequalities about polygonal approximations: (i) inserting points increases or leaves unchanged the polygonal sum; (ii) length > 0 if a<b and γ one-one; (iii) lengths add over subintervals; (iv) orientation reversal preserves length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These observations are used to prove properties of cumulative arc length and to justify reparametrization by arc length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cumulative arc length s(t) and parametrization by arc length (Proposition 3.38)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a rectifiable simple arc γ:[a,b]→R^n define s(t)=`(γ[a,t]). Then s(t) is continuous, strictly increasing with s(a)=0 and s(b)=`(γ), hence has a continuous inverse ω, which yields an orientation-preserving reparametrization ω(s) whose parameter is cumulative arc length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuity proved from left and right using partitions; reparametrization by arc length is essential to define integrals w.r.t. arc length as Riemann integrals on [0,`(γ)].

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence theorem for integrals with respect to arc length (Theorem 3.39)
rubrics_metrics.description: If γ is a rectifiable simple arc and f is a continuous complex-valued function on the image of γ, then there exists a unique complex number ∫_γ f ds characterized by: for every ε>0 there is δ>0 such that any partition P of [a,b] with mesh<δ satisfies |∑_j f(γ(s_j^*))·|γ(t_j)−γ(t_{j−1})| − ∫_γ f ds| < ε.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When γ is reparametrized by cumulative arc length, ∫_γ f ds becomes an ordinary Riemann integral ∫_0^{`(γ)} f(γ(s)) ds. Remarks: geometric interpretation (area under fence for nonnegative f), extends to vector-valued f, proof uses two preliminary lemmas controlling error terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error-control lemmas for arc length integration (Lemmas 3.40 and 3.41)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma 3.40: for ω the inverse of the cumulative arc length, |γ(ω(s)) − γ(ω(s0))| ≤ ` (γ[ω(s),ω(s0)]). Lemma 3.41: given ε>0 there exists δ>0 such that any partition P with mesh<δ satisfies |`(γ) − `(γ(P))| < ε.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These lemmas are used to show uniform control over polygonal approximations and to prove Theorem 3.39; Lemma 3.41 is the special case f≡1 of Theorem 3.39.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tamely behaved (definition and role)
rubrics_metrics.description: A simple arc γ:[a,b]→R^n is 'tamely behaved' if γ is of class C^1 on (a,b) and near each endpoint each entry of γ' has the property of being either bounded below or bounded above (or both).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notion is weaker than assuming γ' continuous on [a,b] and is chosen so the theory in this chapter works; it is sufficient to guarantee rectifiability and to derive Riemann-integral formulas for length and line integrals even when γ' may be unbounded at endpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arc length formula for tamely behaved arcs (Theorem 3.42)
rubrics_metrics.description: If γ is a tamely behaved simple arc then γ is rectifiable and `(γ) = lim_{a0↓a, b0↑b} ∫_{a0}^{b0} |γ'(t)| dt (i.e., length = ∫ |γ'(t)| dt, with endpoint limits as needed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remarks note that the limit is needed because Riemann integrals are not defined for unbounded functions; one often writes the shortcut ∫_a^b |γ'(t)| dt. Proof reduces to bounding polygonal sums by integrals and uses uniform continuity and mean value estimates on subintervals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integral with respect to arc length for C^1 arcs (Corollary 3.43)
rubrics_metrics.description: If γ is tamely behaved (in particular C^1 on (a,b)) and f is continuous on image of γ, then ∫_γ f ds = ∫_a^b f(γ(t)) · |γ'(t)| dt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from reparametrization by cumulative arc length and Theorem 3.42; standard formula used for computations (e.g., area under a surface above a curve).

rubrics_metrics.name: Line integral (existence) for vector fields (Theorem 3.44)
rubrics_metrics.description: If γ is a rectifiable simple arc and F is a continuous vector field on the image of γ, then the line integral ∫_γ F · ds exists and is the unique limit characterized by: for any ε>0 there exists δ>0 such that any partition P with mesh<δ satisfies |∑_j F(γ(t_j^*))·(γ(t_j)−γ(t_{j−1})) − ∫_γ F·ds| < ε.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remarks: this definition is typically formalized using Stieltjes integrals (not developed here); the line integral is invariant under orientation-preserving reparametrizations and changes sign under reversal of orientation; proof omitted in text but relies on bounded variation of component functions when γ is rectifiable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line integral formula for tamely behaved arcs (Theorem 3.45)
rubrics_metrics.description: If γ is tamely behaved and F is continuous on the image of γ, then the line integral is given by the limit ∫_γ F·ds = lim_{a0↓a, b0↑b} ∫_{a0}^{b0} F(γ(t)) · γ'(t) dt, and one customarily writes ∫_γ F·ds = ∫_a^b F(γ(t))·γ'(t) dt (with endpoint limits if γ' unbounded).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reduces line integrals to ordinary Riemann integrals under tamely behaved/C^1 hypotheses; used to compute work by a force field along a curve. The limit is necessary if γ' is unbounded near endpoints; in C^1 on [a,b] case no limit is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parametrization independence and sign under reversal
rubrics_metrics.description: Line integrals computed as limits of the partition sums are independent of the choice of orientation-preserving reparametrization of γ; for the reverse arc −γ the line integral satisfies ∫_{−γ} F·ds = −∫_γ F·ds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shown by relating partition sums under the reparametrization map ϕ and by inspection of approximating sums; important when choosing convenient parametrizations for computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computational niceties and examples (cycloid, quarter circle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples demonstrate reparametrization to avoid unbounded derivatives (e.g., quarter circle using angle parameter), and computation of length and integrals in examples such as the cycloid (explicit s(t) and arch length).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate when derivative may be unbounded yet curve fits theory by reparametrization, show practical use of Corollary 3.43 and Theorem 3.45, and highlight geometric interpretations (area under a fence for ∫ f ds).
